note: Functions N64Recomp refuses (found by running it, see README 'Acceptance'), and what the config does with each. stub: emitted as an empty body (the operation has no host meaning). ignored: not emitted; the runtime must provide a host function of the same name (Phase 1 shim list). Names are inventory names (static population). renamed: emitted as NAME_recomp because NAME collides with a host C/libc declaration (found by compiling the output with clang). instruction: single-word replacements (N64Recomp [[patches.instruction]]); the hand-written codec kernels get their PC with a never-taken `bltzal zero` whose only effect is ra = pc+8, which N64Recomp treats as a call into the inline table; the pair is rewritten to load the same ra value directly (lui/ori), behaviour unchanged. hook: C call inserted by N64Recomp ([[patches.hook]]) at function entry (or before_vram; "site_arg": true passes that vram as a third argument); the runtime (tools/recomp/runtime) defines the callee extern "C".

ignored.osStopThread_rx: libultra osStopThread (inventory osPfsChecker_full, identity.json); the game stops and restarts other threads (music_tempo_set, world_collision_response, func_800E847C, func_800EB028), but N64ModernRuntime's osStopThread only handles the calling thread (assert otherwise, a no-op in release) and the following osStartThread then inserts a running/queued thread into the run queue a second time (self-loop: boot hang). Shim in tools/recomp/runtime/src/shims.cpp.

renamed.modff: host libm modff (conflicting types); emitted as modff_recomp
renamed.memchr: host libc builtin memchr (incompatible redeclaration); emitted as memchr_recomp

hook.why: every compressed code image (game image at boot from game_init, overlay A/B from PrevMaxPath via inflate_decompress) is inflated by inflate_entry(src ROM offset, dst, n); at entry the runtime maps src to the recompiled section (build/recomp/rush2049_images.h) and calls unload_overlays/load_overlays so lookups dispatch to the image being loaded. The inflate itself still runs recompiled and writes the data into rdram.

the idle thread ends in `for (;;) {}` (b . at 0x80002218). ultramodern schedules game threads cooperatively (one runs at a time, switches only inside libultra calls), so a spinning idle thread would hold the CPU forever once every other thread blocks; the hook calls ultramodern pause_self (wait for external events, then run the woken higher-priority thread), as the runtime intends for idle loops.

Phase 2 frame oracle (runtime/src/oracle.cpp): the libultra scheduler's __scExec hands every RSP task to osSpTaskStartGo(&sctask->list) at 0x80000EE4; before it the hook reads the OSScTask pointer from the frame (sp+0x24), and for graphics tasks counts the frame, hashes the display lists and the 8 MiB of rdram, drives the frame-clocked input script and stops after --frames. It runs on the scheduler thread while the other game threads are suspended (ultramodern runs one at a time), so the snapshot is consistent.

busy-wait with no call inside (lh D_8002EB70 (__osScTaskCount, scheduler +0x288) until 0: mode-switch drain when state_word_a != state_word_b (the v1 laptop wall-clock boot hang: 13/13 runs with RT64)); ultramodern switches game threads only inside libultra calls, so the writer (another game thread woken by an SP/DP/VI/AI message) never runs while this spins. rush_hook_spin (runtime/src/hooks.cpp) yields like rush_hook_park_idle (wait <=1 ms for an external message, deliver it, run a woken higher-priority thread); a no-op with --clock frames.
